This release is mostly about security: the programs behind Claude Code and the gateway are checked before they run, and Claude Code's config is checked before it's handed over. It also merges a batch of community fixes.

## Security

- Claude Code only runs if it matches Anthropic's signed manifest. Newly installed versions save the manifest automatically. Older installs without one fetch it first and don't run until they have it.
- The gateway checks the bytes of each file as it loads its own code, so swapping a file after the check doesn't work.
- The gateway now uses its own copy of its runtime (Node, the libraries it needs, and the glibc it starts Claude Code with), kept outside the toolkit and checked against the app package before every start. Package upgrades and toolkit updates don't touch it. The first start copies it from the toolkit, which **takes about 105 MB more space**; if the toolkit's version doesn't match, it's downloaded instead (about 130 MB).
- The app's own helper programs now live inside the app package, and other processes can't debug the gateway or Claude Code or read their memory.
- Claude Code's config (CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, commands, agents, output styles, plugins, MCP servers and auto memory) is scanned for jailbreak patterns before the gateway passes it to Claude Code. If something matches, that turn doesn't run and you're told which file and line. `claude` in the terminal goes through the same checks. Plugin hooks don't run, and skills are invoked as `/user:name`.
- Writing jailbreak content into CLAUDE.md, `.claude/` or the memory folder is blocked by the safety check.
- Usage queries only accept the exact host name.
- See "The code the gateway and Claude Code run" in SECURITY.md for details.

## Fixes

- Saving a file resolves the path before checking the target, so tricks like `/.` don't get around it, and it won't write to something that isn't a regular file.
- A Git project's trust record now covers hook contents, the full config and the gitdir; changing them asks again.
- Components check that a file is a regular file before reading anything you can edit.
- A broken entry in the ledger no longer crashes the gateway.
- Segmented downloads keep writing until every byte is on disk, instead of reporting success after a partial write.
- When the upstream connection is reset, the stream fix still reaches the UI.
- Concurrent sessions no longer collide on temporary thumbnail files.
- "Skip next run" on a scheduled task skips only that run.
- After a config change, ⚡ Send now ends an idle turn instead of getting stuck.
- Forked sessions with the same start time are ordered by creation time.
- App files that couldn't be read at startup are restored too.
- Opening another conversation while a turn is running no longer gets stuck on the config confirmation.
- Fixed several hangs and pointless waits: "Save to", failed silent installs, the update loop, and "Rewind and ask again".

Thanks to zx-5426 for the fixes and the red-team material.

This release tightens several checks in app updates, so upgrading no longer triggers a false "tampering" notice, and fixes a batch of issues found in reviews.

## Updates

- After a new version is installed in the background, the UI and gateway files are laid down again from the new package instead of being treated as "program files modified": no tampering notice, and Claude is not told that someone changed the program. If the files change while the version stays the same, they are still restored and you are still warned.
- A new package must come with a sha256 checksum or it won't be downloaded, and it is checked against that value again right before installing, so a package swapped after download is not installed.
- Besides matching the installed app's signature, the package must also be signed with the cccodroid release certificate.
- Silent installs stop the gateway first; the new version starts it again.

## Fixes

- After tapping "Stop" in the ongoing notification, the UI no longer gets stuck on a page that can't connect. Long-pressing the title to reload now shows "Waiting for gateway", starts the gateway and opens the UI once it's up; if the UI stays disconnected while open, the gateway is started automatically too. This means that tapping "Stop" while the UI is open brings the gateway back within a few seconds; to stop it for good, close the UI first, then tap Stop.
- After jumping to an earlier point from a chapter or bookmark and deleting a message, scrolling down no longer skips unread content.
- Switching to another session right after "Rewind and ask again" no longer overwrites that session's draft with the rewound prompt.
- In a step group you collapsed by hand, tapping an agent on the subagent contact card now expands it and scrolls to it.
- Git: if you write a commit message in another repository while a commit is still running, finishing the first commit no longer clears it.
- Merge: changing a selection while materials are being fetched now uses the new selection instead of putting old material under the new label.
- "View in Lineage": when the target is hidden by a project filter or by "hide misc", the filter that hides it is lifted.
- Reference links: newly opened sessions and newly added chapters are no longer reported as "not found".
- Hooks: if a rule changes or is deleted while you're editing it, your edit is no longer saved onto a different rule; "Pause" now applies to the level you're viewing, so project hooks can be paused too.
- Undoing a config change restores extension files exactly as they were, byte for byte and with their permissions.
- A skill ZIP import that fails halfway no longer leaves an empty folder holding the name.
- Cancelled downloads and previews no longer leave files open; very long file names can be saved and uploaded; pushing a branch whose name starts with HEAD is no longer refused.
- Deleting a scheduled task while it runs still records that run's cost; interrupted runs without a session ID are no longer cleared along with others.
- Moving a session now finishes writes the system only partly completed instead of leaving a truncated file; the self-test summary is shown in full; CPU usage of nested child processes is no longer counted twice.

Thanks to chenshi723 for the review reports.

This is a patch release for 0.6.4 that fixes filing sessions in Lineage.

## Fixes

- In 0.6.3 and 0.6.4, filing and back-filling sessions (Lineage) from Claude's terminal always failed, saying the gateway "could not prove itself". 0.6.3 hardened protection against impersonation, which changed how the gateway proves its identity, and the terminal filing command broke as a result. Terminal tools now have their own way to verify the gateway, so filing and back-filling work again, and the impersonation protection stays in place.
- The "status reconcile" check in the toolchain self-test failed for the same reason and is fixed too.

This release fixes several security issues, asks you to allow Shizuku activation in a system dialog, and fixes a large batch of problems found in reviews and everyday use.

## Security

- Fixed several security issues.
- Activating Shizuku and turning on "activate automatically at boot" now first show a native dialog, and only go ahead when you tap Allow.
- A few settings that need your consent (keep-alive boost, running privileged commands without asking, device tools, WebView debugging, activating Shizuku at boot) are now stored differently. **Turn them on once more after updating.**

## Fixes

- After running for a long time, the gateway log no longer keeps warning about too many listeners (they piled up while replaying the event stream).
- Stopping a turn while `/model`, `/effort` or `/autocompact` is still waiting for the model list no longer changes your settings; it replies that it stopped and nothing changed.
- When a running session is opened from an old chapter or a bookmark, "View" on the confirmation bar first jumps back to the latest and then scrolls to the card.
- A turn with only background tasks left still counts toward the parallel limit, so a new session is no longer told the previous turn hasn't finished.
- Replies received again after a dropped connection show the time taken based on when the turn actually ended.
- When a scheduled task's provider is left empty (follow the project), the model list follows the selected project's provider and changes with it. After provider settings change, old model lists are no longer reused.
- "Other providers" on the Usage page no longer lists the main card's provider again. Signing out clears the usage figures and the weekly quota summary.
- If a file you're editing is renamed, moved or deleted, saving asks whether to save a copy under the original name instead of quietly creating a new file.
- Files opened from project details use the same viewer as the file browser.
- If the source file is saved while an Office conversion is running, the freshly converted PDF still opens.
- The commit message is kept after Select all and after viewing a diff. In a repository with no commits yet, the diff shows the working tree as it is now.
- Diffs, history and commit details no longer fail in sha256 git repositories.
- When sharing, files with apostrophes, tildes and similar characters in the name get the right type.
- If the system reclaims the app while you're choosing where to "Save to", the file is still saved when you come back, with no empty file left behind.
- A brief wireless-debugging disconnect is no longer treated as an unpaired device, so automatic activation isn't switched off.
- Websites in the in-app browser are no longer blocked by the HTML preview's offline switch.
- Scheduled tasks: tasks created during the repeated hour when daylight saving ends aren't counted as missed; queues restored after a restart finish and record usage normally; a successful run cancels pending failure retries; "Skip the next run" also applies to missed runs.
- Attachments uploaded to a new session no longer end up in an empty draft if you switch away.
- A saved prompt close to the size limit no longer disappears right after saving.
- If UI customization or appearance can't be saved, you're told, instead of the change only lasting until restart.
- Importing two fonts back to back no longer applies the interface font to replies.
- While a component is downloading or being verified, the devkit modules it needs can't be removed. Packages you installed by name with `pkg install` are no longer removed along with another package.
- Cancelling a model download no longer lets the file through once verification finishes.
- Switching the same provider to another account's key no longer records the balance difference as spending.
- Custom component descriptions containing colons now produce a valid skill file.
- Lineage: layout carries over across projects; date ticks are right around daylight saving changes; sessions moved into a project no longer show the old location; a last line without a newline is still read.
- Undoing deletes, pinning, renaming and similar changes are now written to disk atomically.
- Interjections and ⚡ now check the run settings too.
- Filled in a batch of missing translations, and fixed the language dropdown and Spanish plurals.
- Toolchain self-test: when the network can't reach Google, or reaches github.com only some of the time, this is now reported as a network limitation instead of a broken tool.
- The help page now lists the Material appearance.

## Other

- The app package now includes the LGPL license and source notice for the glibc loader.
- The docs now include test results from a OnePlus Ace 7 Pro (Android 17).

Thanks to chenshi723 for twelve review reports, to zx-5426 for nine fix PRs, and to a community member for the OnePlus Ace 7 Pro device report.

This release fixes several security issues, stops screen reading from reading password fields, and fixes a batch of problems found in the v0.6.2 review.

## Security

- Fixed several security issues.
- "Confirm sensitive actions" no longer has an off switch and is always on. Its description stays in Settings, and you still allow or deny each action on its card.
- "Pause all hooks" on the Extensions page now sets the rules aside and puts them back unchanged when you resume, so it no longer turns off "Confirm sensitive actions" as well. Hooks you had already paused are moved to the new method automatically after updating, and no rules are lost.
- `claude` run directly in the in-app terminal now also gets "Confirm sensitive actions".
- In safe mode, "Allow everything", "Decide automatically" and "Auto-accept edits" fall back to "Ask each time": hooks don't run in safe mode, so sensitive actions can't be caught on their own.
- Before each turn, the Claude Code program is checked against Anthropic's signed official manifest. If it doesn't match, it isn't started, and you're asked to reinstall it under Settings → Updates. The signed manifest is saved automatically the first time you're online after updating.
- When app files have been modified, they're still restored from the app package, and now the app also tells you once. Claude is also told on its next turn that the change was undone.
- Screen reading no longer reads what's in password fields. The field is still listed and marked as a password field, and Claude can still fill it in when you ask, but can't append to what's already there.

## Fixes

- If the disk fills up or a write fails while saving a file, the original is no longer wiped: the new content goes to a temporary file first and only replaces the original once it's fully written.
- When settings can't be written to disk, you're now told plainly that the change may apply for this run but will revert on restart, instead of it looking saved.
- A full disk during a segmented download no longer takes the whole gateway down; the download just fails.
- Output style files with no space after `name:` had the first letter of the name cut off. Fixed.
- Scheduled tasks:
  - the repeated hour when daylight saving time ends no longer hangs the gateway;
  - the daily limit is checked again right before a run starts, so a task that waited in the queue is skipped if the limit ran out meanwhile;
  - the daily limit no longer goes wrong once the run log gets long;
  - "Test run" uses a fresh session and doesn't affect the session the real runs continue.
- If usage stats are cleared while a backfill is running, the backfill's stale results are discarded instead of being written back.
- Cancelling a message in the middle of a queue no longer stops the later ones from continuing the original session.
- After you switch provider, model or thinking effort, messages are no longer sent to an idle background process still using the old settings.
- If the provider or model is changed elsewhere while `/model`, `/effort` and similar commands are fetching the model list, the command is dropped and you're asked to run it again, rather than writing the old settings back.
- Tool results and failure states no longer go missing when you scroll back through history.
- Numbers of deleted custom providers are never reused for new ones. If deleting a provider fails to save, it's rolled back instead of being half-deleted.
- When two components install a command with the same name at the same time, the second is blocked instead of overwriting the first.
- Checking for updates no longer crashes on Android 8.0 / 8.1.
- Tapping the update notification when the app isn't running now lets you continue the install; the package name and signature are checked again first.
- After a reboot, scheduled task alarms are restored even if Shizuku isn't running yet.
- The first-use confirmation for screen reading and tapping now waits up to 70 seconds, the same as the clipboard.
- Turning the work island off and on quickly no longer leaves two copies.
- A title you set by hand while a backfill is waiting is no longer overwritten.

Thanks to chenshi723 for the v0.6.2 review reports, and to zx-5426 for reporting the output style name parsing issue.

This release fixes several security issues, plus problems that could freeze the app or keep Claude from finding files.

## Switches to turn on again after updating

- "Privileged commands without per-command confirmation", "Enhanced background keep-alive", "Device tools" and the screen-reading mode are all off after the update. Turn them on again in Settings.
- When you turn one on, the system screen-lock prompt appears. Verify, and it stays on after cccodroid restarts; skip it, and it only lasts until the app restarts. This keeps other programs from changing these settings.
- On devices without a screen lock, or below Android 11, these only last until the app restarts.

## Security

- Fixed several security issues.
- After Shizuku is activated, cccodroid turns wireless debugging back off if it turned it on for activation, and stops the adb server it used. The first launch after updating cleans up anything left behind by earlier versions.
- Device tools ask once per session before the first screen read, tap, typing or screenshot.
- In the file panel, committing, discarding, pulling or pushing in a Git repository whose own config would run commands now lists those commands and waits for your confirmation.
- If a project (or a folder above it) contains settings that run automatically when opened, such as hooks or MCP servers, you're asked before the first message. Choose "Don't load" and the turn goes ahead without them; allow, and it's remembered until those settings change. Scheduled tasks never load settings you haven't confirmed.
- UI and gateway files are checked against the app package on every launch and regularly while running, and restored if they've been modified.
- The adb server started from the terminal now uses a socket in the app's private folder instead of 127.0.0.1:5037. If you really need 5037, add `-P 5037` to the command.
- "Network" in HTML preview applies only to the page you allowed; another page needs its own permission.
- Turning on web debugging with `~/.webdebug` from the terminal now asks for confirmation the first time.

## Appearance

- The light "Construct" look now has a paper-tone slider under Settings → Appearance: left is whiter, right is yellower; the default is unchanged. The status bar follows it.
- In the light "Material" look, the docked sidebar no longer leaves two short thin arcs at its top and bottom edges.

## OpenAI API local protocol bridge

- Bridge status is now shown in three parts: component entry, configuration check, and local service. When something fails, it says which step and what to do next, instead of a blanket "back up first".
- When the bridge is running fine but the app's record of its model list or auth style no longer matches, you can review what would change and confirm, and the app syncs it. Only the app's provider record is changed; the address and key stay the same and the bridge isn't restarted.

## Fixes

- Claude's Grep and Glob always came back with "no files found": Claude Code's built-in search program couldn't be launched here, and failed silently. They now use rg from the dev kit, or Claude Code's own copy if the "CLI extras" module isn't installed.

## Viewer

- Tapping "Open as text" on a binary file such as an APK put the whole file into the editor as text, which froze the app until it was force-stopped. Now:
  - APKs, archives, libraries, fonts, and audio/video files no longer offer "Open as text";
  - for files it can't tell by name, the viewer checks the start of the file first and shows a note instead of opening the editor if it's binary. UTF-16 text with a BOM still opens normally.

This release is mostly about privileged commands interrupting you less. It also fixes a few problems in the sidebar and in the background.

## Privileged commands

- Until now, every privileged command needed you to come back to cccodroid and tap Allow, and a task running in the background stopped as soon as it hit one. There are now three ways to loosen this, from narrowest to widest:
  - "Allow, don't ask again for this command for 10 minutes" covers only that exact command.
  - Tick "Allow all later privileged commands in this session" in the prompt, and that session won't be asked again and can keep going in the background. It resets when the app restarts.
  - Settings → Device & permissions → "Stop confirming privileged commands one by one (at your own risk)" runs every privileged command directly. A disclaimer is shown when you turn it on.
- Commands that touch cccodroid itself or Shizuku / Sui are caught and confirmed where possible, but not every form can be caught (for example, one hidden in a script file).
- Sui is supported (#112): if you already have Sui, grant cccodroid access in Sui and you don't need Shizuku.

## Sidebar and sessions

- Sessions filed under Misc no longer disappear from the sidebar while they are pinned, running, or waiting for your confirmation.
- Long sessions could be wrongly filed under Misc by the AI. Now, if a session the AI put in Misc gets compacted once or grows past 512 KB, it goes back to its normal group automatically. Sessions you moved there yourself stay put.
- Local paths written as `[path](file:///…)` links in replies used to show up as raw text you couldn't tap. They now open in the viewer. The model is also told to write paths as plain text instead of wrapping them in links.

## Background

- Swiping cccodroid away in Recents now closes it: if nothing is running, the gateway stops and the ongoing notification goes away, instead of restarting itself and getting stuck on "Starting…". If a turn is running, it stops after the turn finishes. Scheduled tasks are still woken by a system alarm when they're due.

## Other

- Fixed several security issues.
- The work island now receives checklist progress (done / total), so it can draw a segmented progress bar (#111).
- Fixed a few gateway tests that failed in CI (#113).
- The in-app help now covers the new features from this release and the last one.

Thanks to STUTTEFRFIX for the PR, to HydrangeaPurple and chenshi723 for their reports, and to a group member for their troubleshooting report.

This release is mostly fixes. chenshi723 did a full review of v0.5.20 and filed 80-odd findings; all of them are handled here. It also fixes two problems reported in the group chat: background tasks getting stuck, and the gateway crashing on startup.

## Background tasks

- When a turn had finished and only a background task was left (for example an SSH tunnel kept open), new messages could sit in the queue forever, and the stop button said the turn "already ended". You can now send into such a turn directly. If its input has already been closed, "Send now" and Stop end the turn together with its background tasks, the queued message goes out right after, and the answer is not marked as interrupted.
- If messages were still queued when the app last exited, the gateway could crash on restart and lose them. Fixed.

## Switching sessions (#87–#90)

- Step groups and subagent cards you collapsed by hand stay that way when you switch away and back.
- Switching to a running session no longer flashes old content, and context usage no longer leaks between sessions.
- Late replies for subagent transcripts no longer point "jump to" at cards that are gone.

## Review fixes (#95–#110)

The main ones:

- **Runs and usage**: a follow-up turn (from an interjection or a background report) that exits abnormally is no longer reported as a success; API usage is recorded for every result; switching currency converts old spending at the exchange rate; a scheduled task's per-run cost limit is checked after every result and stops the run once exceeded.
- **Scheduled tasks**: "Wi-Fi only" now actually receives the Wi-Fi state, including when a VPN is on; changing the system time zone reschedules tasks in the new zone.
- **Sessions**: moving, forking, restoring or importing no longer leaves half-done state behind when it fails; exported sessions include their archive data (chapter titles, status, volumes).
- **Git**: selective commits no longer include files that weren't shown in the list; staged renames commit completely; discarding a staged new file no longer errors.
- **Files**: symlinked folders open in the file panel; file names ending in a space open correctly; late replies in the editor no longer touch the file you're on.
- **Components and modules**: a component's skill no longer overwrites your own skill of the same name; removing a devkit module checks whether components or pkg packages still need it; an interrupted pkg install picks up where it left off when rerun.
- **Android side**: notifications show failures correctly; the system reclaiming the page renderer no longer takes the whole app down; attachments picked while the screen was recreated are no longer lost; the memory manager stops right away when turned off and lists apps it couldn't stop; two USB devices asking for permission at once no longer interfere; 35 native error messages are now translated.
- The APK now ships Shizuku's MIT license notice.

## Other

- New UI language: Indonesian (machine-translated first draft; corrections welcome).
- The OpenAI API local bridge settings can store several models per key, each with its own context window (#86). This needs the next component release; update it under Components once it's out.

## Known issue

- On one Red Magic phone, reopening the app and starting a new session failed with `Failed to fetch` because the gateway was unreachable; restarting fixed it. The cause isn't known yet. If you hit it, please pack the diagnostic logs from Settings and send them to us.

Thanks to chenshi723 for the review and PR, and to everyone in the group who reported problems.

This release fixes three issues reported in the group chat and on GitHub.

## Permissions and plans

- With "Allow everything" on, if Claude entered plan mode by itself, approving the plan lowered your permission mode to "Ask each time" or "Auto-accept edits". The plan card now has "Approve, keep current mode", which returns just this run to the mode it was in and leaves your global setting alone.

## Steps and images

- A step group with an image in the middle couldn't be collapsed. Now it can.
- When an image path in command output can't be read (for example `/data/adb`, which only root can read, or a file that doesn't exist), the preview no longer leaves a dead path behind, and the step group is no longer held open by it.

## Components

- The local OpenAI API bridge (openai-bridge) is updated to r14. Some upstreams reject the reasoning-effort parameters with a bare `400 Invalid request payload`, which failed the whole turn. The bridge now resends once without those two parameters, and remembers that for later requests (#84). Update it under Components.

This release fixes 30-plus issues from two review reports, and tightens which privileged commands run without asking.

## Chats and messages

- When several chats are interrupted at once, each one now gets its own "Continue" card, and the chat list marks them as interrupted.
- Prompts that start with something like `<div>` no longer vanish from the history.

This release is about faster downloads: big files now come down over several connections at once, and there's one more fallback route when GitHub is slow. The idea came from discussion #15.

## Faster downloads

- The devkit, its modules, component packages, Claude Code and app updates are split into up to four segments fetched in parallel once a file is 16 MB or larger. Routes that throttle each connection gain the most: in our tests the cccodroid.net mirror got three to five times faster and GitHub about half again as fast. How much you gain depends on your network.
- Resuming still works. If the network drops, the system kills the app or the download switches routes partway, each segment picks up where it stopped instead of starting over. A route that can't serve segments falls back to a single connection.

## GitHub fallback route

- When both GitHub and the mirror struggle, the app tries gh-proxy.com as a last resort.
- Whatever the route, every file is still checked against its sha256 and signatures, and a mismatch is thrown away, so a third-party route doesn't weaken security.

## Security and stability fixes

A community member did a careful code review and reported ten problems. All of them are fixed in this release:

- **The trash cleanup API could delete all app data.** A program holding the gateway token could wipe the app's home folder with one crafted request. Tapping "Empty trash" never triggered it. Names that escape their folder are now rejected, and the skill-delete API got the same fix.
- **HTML previews could reach the gateway through the native bridge.** A previewed page could use the in-app browser to open files as the gateway. Files served by the gateway can no longer run scripts, and the in-app browser and pane refuse the gateway's own address.
- **HTML previews could follow symlinks out of the preview folder.** The real path is now checked.
- **A crafted token could crash the gateway.** It is now simply rejected.
- **Chinese text or emoji occasionally turned into � while streaming.** A character split across two chunks wasn't reassembled; output is now decoded as a stream.
- **Attaching two files with the same name in the same second overwrote the first.** The second one is now renamed.
- **The editor's conflict check could miss a change made while a save was being received.** It now compares after the whole body arrives.
- **An interjection could be lost if the app was force-stopped before it was delivered.** It is now saved right away and comes back to the queue on the next launch.
- **A Claude Code update that failed its test run left you without a working version.** The new version is now tested before it's switched in.
- **Importing an archive that expands to a huge size could take down the gateway.** There is now a size limit.

**Skill import** is also fixed: every skill in an archive is installed, you can pick several files at once, archives forwarded from chat apps are no longer greyed out in the file picker, and a single SKILL.md can be imported directly.

## Fallback sources for downloading Claude Code

On some networks the official Claude Code download can't be reached, or drops halfway. First install and in-app updates now switch sources automatically:

- The official server is tried first. If it can't be reached or drops twice in a row, the app moves on to npmmirror, Tencent Cloud and the official npm registry in turn, resuming what was already downloaded. Whichever source worked last time is tried first next time.
- It's the same program either way: Anthropic also publishes Claude Code on npm, and these mirrors simply sync it.
- Wherever it comes from, the file has to match the **SHA-256 in Anthropic's official manifest** before it's installed. If the official manifest can't be reached either, the app uses the copy on cccodroid.net, which carries Anthropic's signature and is only used once that signature checks out.
- If even that copy can't be reached, the app checks npm's own registry signature, installs, and re-checks against the official manifest automatically once it's reachable again.
- The npm package is compressed, under half the size of the official direct download, so it's often faster too.

## Fixed: updating the app and the toolchain together left the toolchain "up to date" but still old

**What happened**: when the app and the development toolchain were updating at the same time, the app finished first and restarted the process, cutting off the toolchain download. After the restart, the new app used **its own built-in toolchain version** as the "installed version", so the old toolchain was shown as the new one. Confirmed on a device: what was actually installed was still devkit-2026.10.13.2 (the build before the jmod fix).

This release reworks the whole update chain:

- **Version detection**: the installed version is identified only by the content hash recorded at install time, never guessed from the app's built-in version. Installs without a record are shown as "unknown" with a suggestion to update once. Toolchains installed from a local file now have their hash recorded too.
- **Ordering**: while the toolchain is downloading or being replaced, the app update waits for it. A downloaded toolchain is installed when the app restarts, regardless of the auto-update switch.
- **Checked before replacing**: the tar hash from the release manifest is checked while unpacking; on mismatch the unpacked copy is discarded and the old toolchain is left untouched. A downloaded archive is also re-checked right before it replaces anything.
- **Recoverable replacement**: if a replacement is interrupted (app restart, process killed, battery died), the next launch finishes it or rolls back — no half-installed state. Tested on a device: killed during first-run setup, it completed on relaunch and verified clean.
- **Verify / Repair**: the toolchain now ships a per-file manifest. **Verify** in Settings checks every file's hash (35,068 files in about 4 seconds on the test device); if anything is missing or damaged, **Repair** reinstalls the same version and keeps what you installed with pip / npm -g. A quick check also runs at each launch and notifies you about missing files. Files rewritten during first-run setup (such as git-delta's completion scripts) are recorded into the local baseline by their actual content, so they are not reported as damaged.

**After upgrading**: open the app; Settings will show a toolchain update (devkit-2026.10.14.1) — update when prompted. The jmod fix arrives with it.

## Security fix (update recommended)

The gateway used to listen on 127.0.0.1 with no authentication. On Android that is not a security boundary: any app on the device with network permission, and any web page in the phone's browser, could send it requests — and `/api/chat` defaults to bypassPermissions, which amounts to arbitrary command execution on the device (and, with Shizuku installed, a path to the shell identity).

- On first start the gateway generates a 256-bit access token (stored in the app's private directory, mode 0600); `/api/*` requires it, otherwise 403
- Host is checked (blocks DNS rebinding, 421) and Origin is checked (blocks cross-site requests from web pages, 403)
- The app's UI sends the token automatically, so nothing changes for you; the token survives restarts
- Logging of rejected requests is rate-limited

## Other

- seccomp shim: a foreign SIGSYS (e.g. `kill -SYS`) is no longer swallowed and gets the default action

Open the app once after updating; old UI sessions switch to the token automatically.

### Highlights
- Official, unmodified Claude Code (downloaded from Anthropic's official channel and verified against the official sha256 manifest) with a GUI: streaming output, thinking, file browser, session history; you can interject while it works without interrupting the current turn

- **Automatic updates** (on by default; can be turned off or checked manually): Claude Code updates silently; new cccodroid versions are downloaded, signature-checked and offered for install (installed silently when idle if Shizuku is available); the toolchain is pre-downloaded on Wi‑Fi and swapped in at the next launch, keeping whatever you installed with pip / npm -g
- **One-tap Shizuku install and activation**: Settings downloads the official Shizuku (signing certificate verified) and installs it; activation goes through Wireless debugging with no computer, the pairing code is entered in a notification pinned to the top of the screen, and Shizuku re-activates automatically after a reboot (Wi‑Fi required)
- In the terminal, `priv '<cmd>'` runs commands as the shell user; `usb-adb` debugs another device over OTG; `cccodroid-selftest` exercises 71 tools one by one
- Background-freeze detection: when the system freezes the app, Settings tells you where to allow background running

- arm64 only; needs about 4 GB of free space

- First install downloads about 830 MB; direct GitHub downloads from mainland China measured about 1 MB/s
